title: Machine-learning MIRA-29 score predicts neurological outcome after cardiac arrest
summary: MIRA-29 was derived on a prospective cohort of 1099 out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients (85, 7.7%, had a favorable neurological outcome), with machine learning and genetic algorithms used to optimize a model from five candidate variables, and age was not retained in the final model. External validation on 82,696 patients from the French national registry gave precision 0.86, recall 0.88, accuracy 0.88 and specificity 0.99 for poor neurological outcome. The score uses four simple prehospital variables; prospective clinical validation of its effect on decisions is still needed.
ai_technology: Machine learning and genetic algorithms used to optimize a four-variable prehospital neurological prognosis score
organization: INSERM; Université de Bretagne Occidentale; Laboratoire de Traitement de l'Information Médicale

evidence.tested: Derivation on 1099 prospective patients and external validation on 82,696 registry patients.
evidence.unknown: Impact on clinical decision-making; the machine-learning step optimizes a score built from simple variables; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning and genetic algorithms optimized the score model.
